plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no benefit to shading your bid up or down. With my value at $8, bidding exactly $8 maximizes my expected profit: I win only when profitable (my value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down - overbidding risks winning at a loss, underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $42, so I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. Since my value is $13, bidding $13 ensures I only win when it's profitable (i.e., when my value exceeds the second-highest bid) and I never overpay. There's no strategic advantage to shading my bid in this format.
